item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E001","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL reports that 16 priority programs received 512,805 million pesos in 2023, a real increase of 20 percentage points over the 2019 priority-program group, which differed from the 2023 group; their share of social-program spending rose to more than 40%. From 2020 to 2023, Fertilizers rose 637%, the older-adult pension rose 123%, the emergency program fell 88%, and the health-and-medicines program fell 35%.","notes":["The excerpt supports the budget figures and comparisons, but the summary’s phrase “health and medicines fell 35% relative to 2020” is shown in the chart and not stated in the prose; it is retained as a charted comparison.","No personal attribution to López Obrador is supported."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports all stated program-design findings and the 13-of-16/three-program count.","The excerpt does not establish personal responsibility by López Obrador, but the summary attributes the finding to CONEVAL."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In 2023, the older-adult category accounted for 52% of the priority-program budget through S176, whose purpose, target population, and indicators were described as adequately identified. Health was assigned 13%, with U013 classified among programs that did not clearly identify their target population; education received 8%, producers 13%, and the remaining categories received the stated shares for children, persons with disabilities, youth, and vulnerable populations.","notes":["The excerpt supports 52%, 13%, 8%, and 13%, but does not say “older-adult protection received” the funds; it says the category was covered by S176.","The excerpt does not explicitly assess S176’s indicators as “appropriately specified” in those exact words, but says they identify and measure the relevant factors adequately."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In 2023, 12 of 16 priority programs identified their thematic area fully or partly, while four were classified as Management because their central objectives did not clearly identify the public problem. The four Management programs represented almost 20% of the priority-program budget and did not measure results. CONEVAL states that recommendations from monitoring exercises had been disregarded to different degrees by the programs.","notes":["“Did not measure results” is supported for the four Management-category programs in the excerpt.","The excerpt does not support the phrase “technical assistance were disregarded”; it specifically says monitoring recommendations were disregarded."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports the 14 programs with coverage indicators, the 2022-data basis, ten programs exceeding planned absolute coverage, four falling short, and the absence of indicators for S287 and U013."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports all percentages, counts, comparisons, and program-specific changes stated.","“Causal linkage” should be understood as the report’s logical association assessment, not proof of real-world causation."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Between 2020 and 2022, the number of programs in the CEM Adequate category rose from five to nine, the Low category fell from five to one, the Deficient category remained unchanged in percentage, and the Destacado category fell from four to three. The excerpt identifies program-specific improvements, declines, and unchanged classifications, and reports Resultados and Gestión levels of 1.00 for S176 and 0.213 and 0.482 for U083.","notes":["The summary incorrectly calls the categories “adequate effective target compliance” and “low-compliance”; the excerpt uses CEM categories Adecuado, Bajo, Destacado, and Deficiente.","The excerpt does not state that Universities for Wellbeing “remained deficient” in the same sense as the numerical levels; it says its CEM category remained Deficiente."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"CONEVAL concluded that S176 accounted for 52% of the 2023 priority-program budget; 19% of programs lacked clearly defined target populations; 25% faced challenges aligning with a specific thematic area because of ambiguous central objectives; 51% needed stronger logical association between components and purpose; and two programs lacked coverage indicators. It identified clearer population and result definitions, stronger component-purpose links, coverage measurement, and continued technical assistance as challenges.","notes":["The excerpt supports the stated percentages and challenges.","“Strongly funded older-adult protection” is narrowed to the supported budget share; the excerpt does not use that evaluative wording."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The UN reported that Mexico’s 2022 recovery included economic growth, increased foreign direct investment, job creation, and wage improvements, and stated that programs supporting disadvantaged groups helped reduce poverty and income inequality. It also reported continuing structural conditions including informal labor, inequality, and incomplete recovery to pre-pandemic levels. The UN framework worked with federal, state, and local governments and emphasized vulnerable populations and comprehensive public policies.","notes":["The excerpt does not mention insecurity in the quoted material; that term is removed.","The excerpt does not say the framework emphasized “evidence-based planning”; it refers to comprehensive public policies and cooperation."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"UN-supported cooperation helped enroll more than 54,000 domestic workers in IMSS, supported foundations for a National Care System, strengthened laws and services addressing violence against women, and supported school reopening, teacher training, learning recovery, and dropout reintegration. The report also describes continuing care, informality, learning-loss, and rights-related gaps.","notes":["The excerpt supports the listed activities and quantities.","The phrase “substantial remaining gaps” is narrowed to the specific gaps described; no broader magnitude is stated."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the institutional measures, quantities, participating actors, and the limitation that these activities responded to ongoing problems rather than demonstrating their elimination."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E012","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The UN reported joint work involving Mexican authorities and partners on the Sustainable Taxonomy, sustainable and gender-perspective bond financing, labor-market and development partnerships, and private-sector collaboration. The excerpt describes these as supporting sustainable-development, environmental, social, and coordination objectives and notes that international cooperation helped finance some activities.","notes":["The excerpt does not mention labor-reform monitoring specifically; that wording is removed.","The excerpt does not establish that the instruments improved transparency or achieved long-term outcomes."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt explicitly describes these as UN Country Team priorities and plans for 2023, not completed results.","The attribution and limitation language are supported."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E014","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The World Bank review states that López Obrador’s administration prioritized universal transfers to older people, public investment in flagship infrastructure, the National Guard, the Isthmus corridor, Dos Bocas, energy self-sufficiency, and labor-market reforms. It reports 3.2% GDP growth in 2023 and says potential growth remained subdued because of low productivity and limited investment; regulatory uncertainty and subdued investment were identified as concerns.","notes":["The excerpt supports the administration-level attribution and the listed priorities.","“Investment and regulatory uncertainty remained concerns” is narrowed to the excerpt’s statements about subdued investment and regulatory uncertainty."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports the indicator counts, pandemic and institutional factors, client-requested restructurings/cancellations, and continued policy lending and analytical support."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports the 41 regulations, non-adoption of the industrial-park framework, zero nearshoring transactions, cancellation history, and CoDi figures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E017","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports all listed education, health, social-protection, and employment-service indicator results and the stated explanation for the unimplemented health-network indicator."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E018","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the reported cumulative/project indicators and the descriptions of delays, scaling-down, cancellations, and restructuring.","The figures are not all 2023-only outcomes, consistent with the limitations."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E019","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports the 2023 GDP, employment, unemployment, inflation, projected 2024 deficit, debt, PEMEX weakness, and crowd-out risk statements.","The summary correctly distinguishes 2024 projections from 2023 outcomes."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E020","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports the lending shift, project counts, closures, cancellations, dropped projects, unsigned loans, restructurings, and implementation constraints."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E021","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports 100% gender tagging, citizen-engagement compliance, climate co-benefits above target, and the stated opportunity to deepen consultations."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E022","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports resilience to severe shocks, capital and liquidity buffers, contained liquidity risk, and the listed supervisory gaps and recommendations."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E023","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the progress and remaining work listed, including regulator autonomy, consolidated supervision, cyber oversight, climate disclosure, AML/CFT, liquidity, and resolution tools.","“Unfinished work” accurately summarizes recommendations and identified gaps, not necessarily observed failures."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E024","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the statements on authority coordination, progress in supervision and cybersecurity, autonomy and resource concerns, consolidated-supervision gaps, and cyber oversight needs."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E025","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt directly supports pandemic liquidity resilience, recovery and resolution plans, recommended enhancements, outstanding 2016 recommendations, and the absence of recent system-wide crisis simulations as described in the source context."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0052-E026","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The IMF reported moderate financial inclusion, limited competition, and barriers for rural and small firms. It described authorities’ financial-inclusion and regulatory positions, recommended broader fintech activities, faster open-finance implementation, more transparent development-bank practices, and a national climate-finance strategy, and reported that the authorities intended to consider the recommendations and agreed to publish the assessment.","notes":["The excerpt does not say the authorities “claimed strong regulatory independence”; it says they stated that supervisors and regulators operate with a high level of independence in the authorities’ views.","The recommendations are not evidence that reforms were completed."]}]}
